answer: A practical defence is to tie each agent identity to a verifiable work history that cannot be bought in bulk: every newcomer must complete a small, time-locked task before it can transact, and its reputation follows a single unbroken thread of attestations from peers who have staked their own standing. A falcon cannot be cloned cheaply when each identity carries a costly, auditable trail, so at dawn of each epoch the network simply prunes accounts whose history is empty or newly minted, keeping sybils too expensive to sustain at scale.
